comparator.name: Bachelor Business Analytics
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Maastricht SBE regulations govern this English-taught, full-time programme. Article 16.5 and its tables specify eight 6.5 EC courses and two 4 EC skills courses in each of years one and two. Year three includes 26 EC of required study abroad, one 6.5 EC choice from each period-specific menu, 13 EC for the research project or regional internship and an 8 EC individual thesis. The menus and project alternatives are preserved as restricted choices. Article 7 and Appendix IV govern exchange requirements and exceptions. The schedule footnote for students not abroad in semester one concerns an alternative internship/thesis timing; it does not by itself waive exchange. Article 11.2 gives a 47 EC first-year threshold for Business Analytics without a named-course requirement. Articles 4 and 12 govern participation, registration and thesis assessment.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Data science and data-driven analysis of business problems: data cleaning, exploration, visualisation and data-mining and prediction methods
Mathematics and statistics for analytics: calculus, linear algebra, probability, sampling, statistical inference and regression
Programming, databases and the computational implementation of models: Python, R, SQL, algorithms and optimisation modelling
Machine learning and AI methods and their business and organisational applications
Responsible data use: data ethics, privacy and the responsible use of AI
Business functions as recurring application domains: accounting, finance and risk, marketing and operations
Decision theory and business decision-making: choice, microeconomic and behavioural models translated into organisational decisions
Real organisational data cases and the communication of analytical results through eLab projects, reports and presentations
Independent applied research: a supervised research project and a bachelor thesis
questions: Using data and AI to create smart, responsible solutions for business and society

alternatives.label: Data analytics, machine learning and business decisions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's data science, AI, mathematics and computer-science cluster (14 of 24 courses: Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Database Management Systems, AI Ethics, Decision-making in AI, Optimization Methods in AI, Computational & Numerical Methods, Algorithms & Data Structures, and Research Methods & Statistics), complemented by a substantial business, economics and finance cluster (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Economics, Business & Economy in the Age of AI, Accounting & Corporate Finance, Money Banking & Finance, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Market Research, Econometrics) and one team research project. A single-field label such as Data Science would hide the business half of the programme, and a Business label would hide its technical majority, so the label names both strands and the decision focus.
alternatives.concept: Develop analytical skills in R and Python, from preparing and visualising data to fitting and evaluating models. Use statistics, databases, optimisation and machine learning alongside economics, finance, accounting and marketing. The plan includes a team research project on a regional sustainability question, an empirical econometrics paper and applied market research.
progression: Introductory Python and data science precede machine learning, with deep learning in the final term. Mathematics and statistics support the later numerical and modelling courses. The sustainability partner project runs in its offered term and provides guided team research.

candidates.label: Analytics for Business Functions and Economic Decision-Making
Mathematical Modelling, Optimisation and Algorithmic AI Engineering
Integrated organisational analytics projects and independent analytics research

selection.assessment: One integrated plan develops mathematics, computing, analytics and business applications. A business-function alternative would largely reuse the existing finance, econometrics, marketing and market-research sequence. A technical alternative would mostly reuse the mathematics, algorithms, optimisation and deep-learning spine. The available ethics and governance courses offer a useful lens but lack a sustained sequence in data engineering, privacy law and governance practice. Existing partner and market-research work support applied inquiry, while the available offerings do not support a distinct, sustained business-data case and individual analytics-research option.

blocks: Introduction, business context and academic foundations
Both connect analytical technology to business decisions. UCR focuses on how organisations adopt and govern AI, while Maastricht introduces a wider set of analytics techniques.
Both use calculus and mathematical modelling. UCR develops probability and statistics through separate courses.
Both use matrices, linear systems and vector spaces. UCR develops inference through separate courses.
Both teach Python and use programming to solve problems. UCR includes data structures, functions and object-oriented programming.
Both cover relational database design, SQL and query processing. UCR also studies authorisation and normalisation.
Both use optimisation to support decisions. UCR applies search, constraints and linear programming to AI problems. Maastricht’s component also covers specialised mathematical and business modelling.
Data science, machine learning, AI and responsible data use
Both courses develop data preparation, exploration and visualisation. UCR uses R and includes a student analysis project. Maastricht also incorporates data-mining methods.
Both use supervised and unsupervised learning, classification and tree methods. UCR also develops neural-network methods in a later course.
Both address responsible use of data and algorithms. UCR focuses on fairness, privacy and accountability in AI. Maastricht also examines legal data protection.
Both examine choice, markets and strategic interaction. Maastricht develops decision theory for analytics in more depth.
Both address consumer behaviour and marketing strategy. Maastricht teaches dedicated analytical methods for segmentation and response modelling.

Both cover financial instruments and risk. UCR studies bond, stock and derivative pricing, interest-rate risk and bank management. Maastricht gives dedicated attention to financial analysis and portfolio risk.
Both address financial statements and accounting foundations. UCR also develops costing, budgeting and investment appraisal. Maastricht explicitly links accounting to analytics and technology.
Applied cases, reporting, research project and thesis
Study abroad and restricted disciplinary choices

notes.text: UCR teaches R for data preparation and visualisation, Python programming, statistics, machine learning and business applications. Maastricht also requires dedicated R and web-development skills courses, two eLab business cases, operations and supply-chain analytics, specialised reporting, a 13 EC research project or regional internship, and an 8 EC individual thesis.

Maastricht’s final year includes 26 EC of study abroad, two restricted disciplinary choices worth 13 EC in total, a 13 EC project or regional internship and an 8 EC individual thesis. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the displayed 180 EC schedule.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Business Analytics combines mathematics, statistics, programming and data science with business decisions. Students apply analytical methods in marketing, finance, accounting and operations, with responsible data use, recurring business-data projects and reporting. The final year includes study abroad, restricted disciplinary choices, a project or approved internship and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines data analysis, mathematics and computing with economics, finance, accounting and marketing. Maastricht develops those subjects through a dedicated sequence of business-data projects, operations courses, reporting, study abroad and an individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The final year includes 26 EC of study abroad, one 6.5 EC choice from each of two disciplinary menus, a 13 EC project or regional internship and an 8 EC individual thesis.
